prior_coverage:
Nobody has swept publishing as a family before. A grep of docs/, research/ (excluding rendered/), MISSION.md and logs/CHANNEL_LOOP.md for kdp, kindle, ebook, lulu, leanpub, e-vrit, draft2digital, kobo, play books, apple books, smashwords, publishdrive and streetlib finds no prior verdict on Google Play Books, Leanpub, Lulu, Draft2Digital, Kobo, Apple Books or e-vrit. What the repo does already hold:
(1) KDP's AI disclosure rules, snippet grade and sourced only from vendor blogs: research/colony-sweep/scouts/licensing-ip--ai-output-rights.md:121-134. It says "an unblocked agent should open Amazon's own KDP content-guidelines page".
(2) docs/INCOME_PLAN.he.md:100 says KDP requires disclosure and caps titles at 3 per day, and that "תוכן בכמות מת כאסטרטגיה" (bulk content is dead as a strategy).
(3) docs/INCOME_PLAN.he.md:266 rejects Google Play APPS ($25, 12 testers for 14 days). That is the Play Console, not the Play Books Partner Center, so the rejection does not reach Play Books. The same line rejects Envato over its AI ban.
(4) Cold-start precedent. Gumroad's Discover shows nothing until a first sale (research/colony-sweep/audits/storefronts.md:63-77), and MISSION.md:200 records that platform search ranks on prior success. The Gumroad median is $72/month and 44% of products earn $0 (research/colony-sweep/scouts/storefronts--gumroad.md:135-136, snippet).
(5) docs/REJECTED.md:174: charging for a free answer violates the constitution. That rules out repackaging public-domain or state-published text.
(6) Supply cap. MISSION constraint 6 bounds how many distinct honest titles exist (roughly 5 to 15 that the colony could honestly write from its own verified work), so "many listings" here means many venues per title, not many titles.

New evidence this session:
- Leanpub's API (publish, preview, job_status and book info) is used from public repos: tebeka/forging-python Makefile, Just-Understanding-Data-Ltd/compound-engineering-book scripts/publish.sh, and siy/coding-technology. Grade: github. A snippet says the API is a Pro (paid) membership feature.
- Every KDP automation on GitHub drives the browser with Puppeteer or Playwright and types the account credentials; none uses an API (d1fmarketing/book-automation kdp-publisher.js, sabbonzo/kdp-autopublish, victorpreston/amazon_kdp_upload_automation). Grade: github.
- A public script that claims a "Google Play Books Partner API" calls booksApi.volumes.insert(). That method does not exist: GitHub code search of googleapis/google-api-nodejs-client src/apis/books/v1.ts returns 0 hits for Params$Resource$Volumes$Insert, against 1 hit for the control Params$Resource$Volumes$Useruploaded$List. Grade: github. That script is fabricated and must not be cited as a route.
- Draft2Digital refuses content that is wholly AI-generated without extensive human editing, and refuses AI nonfiction from authors without credentials (snippet). Kobo Writing Life's terms prohibit wholly or partly AI-generated content (snippet).

candidates.venue: Google Play Books Partner Center (ebooks, ONIX / automated content fetching)
candidates.what_we_would_list: A small catalogue of honest reference ebooks (EPUB, English and Hebrew) built from the colony's own verified, cited work. Examples: a PCN874 developer reference (the ITA 2009 circular cited line by line, plus the test fixtures); a data.gov.il field guide; licence-gated OWID data explainers. AI authorship is declared in every description. No puzzle-book factory and no public-domain repackaging (docs/REJECTED.md:174). Realistic supply is 5-15 titles in 12 months (MISSION constraint 6).
candidates.existing_product: products/pcn874/docs/SPEC.md (660 lines, cited reference), products/apify-il-open-data/src/dictionary.ts (field dictionary), products/chart-explainer (figures and pages after the licence gates in research/faceless-youtube/DATASETS.md)
candidates.listings_per_owner_step: One Partner Center account plus one payments profile (1-2 owner steps) unlocks every title. If automated content fetching is enabled, new titles and updates flow from our own HTTPS or SFTP host with no further owner action. No per-account title cap was found (UNKNOWN).
candidates.prior_verdict: None. docs/INCOME_PLAN.he.md:266 rejects Google Play apps (Play Console $25 plus 12 testers). That is a different product and does not cover Play Books.
candidates.reopen_basis: Not previously swept. This is a new venue, not a reopen.

gate_zero_cost.evidence: The help centre has a 'Revenue Split FAQs' page (answer 9331459), which implies commission taken from sales. No sign-up or listing fee appeared in any snippet, but the absence of a fee was not read on a primary page. ISBNs: UNKNOWN whether a free Google identifier is still issued.

gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: Google pays partners' bank accounts in supported countries, and countries marked with a star are paid by wire in USD (snippet from answer 3250840 / 6009580). Whether Israel is in the partner payout list (table 6052428) was not seen. Whether the payments-profile identity check involves a camera is UNKNOWN.

gate_programmatic_listing.evidence: From 'Send your books to Google Play with automated content fetching' (answer 2763162, snippet): 'Publishers and service providers who use this content fetching system only need to make their content accessible via an HTTP/HTTPS/SFTP/FTP/Google Cloud Storage server'. ONIX feeds overwrite Partner Center settings, and there is an 'Add multiple books' page (answer 3289689). Caveat: whether fetching is open to a new individual account or must be requested is UNKNOWN. Warning: the only GitHub 'Partner API' script (d1fmarketing/book-automation google-play-publisher.js) calls volumes.insert, which does not exist in the googleapis Books v1 client (github code search, 0 hits vs 1 for a control method).

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: The snippet summary found no blanket ban on AI-generated books in the Publisher Content Policies (answer 1067634). Spam, misleading content and poor user experience are prohibited, and automated models detect violations. No AI disclosure field was found. A Google Play community thread shows buyers complaining about AI books surfacing in suggestions.

gate_buyer_supply.evidence: This is Google's consumer ebook store, with 'Sell books internationally' and a 'Supported countries for selling books on Google Play' table (snippet titles). It brings its own buyers, but no buyer or traffic numbers were found. Whether it has an Israeli storefront or Hebrew-reader demand is UNKNOWN.

candidates.discovery_needs_prior_sale: UNKNOWN at primary grade; no Play Books ranking source was found. Repo precedent (MISSION.md:200): three platforms' search all rank on prior success. Assume cold start: day-one titles surface only on exact-title and niche queries.
candidates.owner_step: (1) Create a Google Play Books Partner Center account under the brand's publisher name (payee in the owner's legal name). (2) Set up the Google payments profile, bank account and tax info. (3) Once only: generate SFTP or content-fetch credentials, or approve the fetch URL. After that, titles are agent-published.
candidates.estimate_basis: Inference. 5-15 honest titles by month 12, times 0-1 sales per title per month, times roughly ₪15-25 net per sale (list price $4.99-9.99 at an unread revenue split). The cold-start shape comes from the Gumroad snippet data (median $72/month; 44% of products at $0; storefronts--gumroad.md:135-136). No Play Books base rate was found.
candidates.time_to_first_sale: UNKNOWN. Inference: 1-4 months after the owner steps and the first successful fetch, and only if a stranger finds a niche title. Month one is most likely ₪0.

gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: KDP pays by EFT, check or wire depending on where the bank is (snippet, help topic GJD7DFFX6X88AK46). There is a 'Payment Service Provider Program FAQ' (GD9NN4LS8ZDU8XZ7) and a KDP community thread titled 'Receiving Royalties Payment to an Israeli Foreign Author', neither read. gate_programmatic_listing.evidence: No public listing API was found. Every GitHub automation is browser automation that types the account credentials: d1fmarketing/book-automation kdp-publisher.js uses Puppeteer with page.type('#ap_password', ...); sabbonzo/kdp-autopublish is 'Amazon KDP automation with Playwright'; victorpreston/amazon_kdp_upload_automation is the same kind. So each title needs an owner click, or the owner's Amazon credentials and 2FA handed to a bot. Both break the brief, and the ToS position on automated access is UNKNOWN.

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: AI-generated content is allowed. Disclosure is a required field in the submission flow; it is internal to Amazon and not shown to buyers; non-disclosure leads to removal (licensing-ip--ai-output-rights.md:121-134, snippet from vendor blogs). A 3 titles/day cap applies (INCOME_PLAN.he.md:100). Hebrew: ebooks in Hebrew are supported; Hebrew paperbacks need a PDF interior and are not eligible for Expanded Distribution (snippet, help topic GML3FXP998V8WS4U).

gate_buyer_supply.evidence: Amazon is the largest ebook and print marketplace, which is background knowledge. No buyer numbers were read, and Hebrew-book demand on Amazon is UNKNOWN.
